key_insight: The paper quantifies how individual modules and their pairwise interactions in the PSO-X modular framework drive optimization performance, showing that interactions can be as influential as single modules and therefore must be considered when configuring or automating PSO algorithms.
problem_solved: Addresses the combinatorial complexity of selecting and configuring dozens of interchangeable PSO-X modules by identifying which modules and interactions most affect solver performance, so users and automated design systems can focus on the most consequential components.
method: Systematic, large-scale evaluation of PSO-X configurations across benchmark continuous optimization problems to gather performance data.
Statistical analysis and variance decomposition to attribute performance variance to individual modules and to interaction terms.
Ranking and sensitivity analysis to identify high-impact modules and interaction patterns that explain most performance differences.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners and AutoML systems to prioritize critical modules and interactions, reducing search space and improving the efficiency of algorithm configuration for continuous optimization tasks.
visual_elements: Heatmap of variance explained: modules on one axis, interactions on the other, color-coded by contribution to performance variance.
Bar chart ranking modules by their individual effect size with annotated cumulative variance captured.
Network diagram of top pairwise interactions showing strength and direction (positive/negative) of interaction effects.
Pipeline diagram illustrating the experimental workflow: configuration sampling → benchmarking → statistical attribution → prioritized module set.
paper_title: Quantifying the Impact of Modules and Their Interactions in the PSO-X Framework
paper_authors: Christian L. Camacho-Villalón, Ana Nikolikj, Katharina Dost, Eva Tuba, Sašo Džeroski
